laravel_adaptation.visibility: The control renders only when the active tenant is present in the authenticated frontend context, the Sites route contract is exact, tenant.view is present, and resolveCapability confirms sites.view.

security_boundary.authentication: Both source and destination Laravel workspace routes use auth middleware.
security_boundary.tenant_context: Both routes use tenant.context; foreign tenant slugs fail closed.
security_boundary.permission: The source requires execution.view. The destination requires tenant.view and sites.view, and the frontend hides the navigation when those destination capabilities are unavailable.
security_boundary.tenant_derived_url: The destination is generated from context.tenant.slug rather than a raw cross-tenant identifier or global /sites path.
security_boundary.mutation: No API request, mutation hook, persistence write, or external WordPress call is introduced.

acceptance_tests: variants/laravel-aiwmweb/backend/tests/Feature/SiteOperationsSitesLinkTerminalityTest.php — binds the exact PENDING canonical row to the production control, proves tenant-derived destination and capability gating, verifies source/alias/destination route contracts, and proves permission/foreign-tenant fail-closed behavior.
Static production wiring assertions prove the control is rendered only from the Site Operations workspace and carries the exact canonical operation marker.

terminality.basis: The canonical Site Operations /sites navigation is implemented as a real tenant-scoped, permission-aware Laravel route transition with no fake success or mutation path.

scope_exclusions: No Site Operations filter, reload, export, details, reliability, or maintenance operation is claimed
No generated parity ledger or reconciliation artifact is manually edited
